RESUMEN

Después de más de una década de espera, Rockstar por fin ha lanzado su juego más ambicioso: Grand Theft Auto 6. Un videojuego que pretende simular absolutamente todo. Desde cometer delitos y protagonizar persecuciones hasta hacer la compra, pescar o montar los muebles de tu apartamento. Con Lucia y Jason como protagonistas, una pareja de criminales inspirada en Bonnie y Clyde, nos adentramos en una nueva Vice City y en un mundo abierto de dimensiones absurdas. Pero ¿estamos realmente ante el mejor videojuego de la historia o el hype se nos ha ido un poquito de las manos?

Lo que está claro es que GTA 6 es un hito tecnológico. Un mundo gigantesco, una densidad de detalles enfermiza, NPCs que parecen tener vida propia, eventos aleatorios por todas partes y una cantidad de sistemas interactuando entre sí que cuesta creer que todo esto funcione en una consola. A eso se suman una historia con personalidad, un apartado audiovisual espectacular y una evolución de las mecánicas de Rockstar que llevan el realismo a un nivel completamente nuevo. Aunque tanta ambición también tiene su precio: un ritmo mucho más lento, controles algo torpes, decisiones de diseño discutibles y una experiencia que a veces parece querer jugarse sola.

Y luego está la forma en la que Rockstar ha decidido vendernos todo esto: versiones recortadas, precios desorbitados, suscripciones, ausencia de formato físico y un rendimiento limitado a 30 FPS. GTA 6 es una barbaridad, probablemente uno de los mejores videojuegos jamás creados, pero eso no significa que sea perfecto ni que tengas que comprarlo a cualquier precio. En esta review repasamos lo mejor, lo peor y todo lo que necesitas saber antes de dejarte el sueldo en Vice City. Porque puede que estemos ante el juego que marcará la próxima década… Y también ante uno de los mayores ejercicios de hype de la historia.

snippet.title: Thanksgiving’s Dark Truth 🇺🇸😥💔  #facts #history  #thanksgiving
snippet.description:
You were taught a lie about Thanksgiving.

The picture is Pilgrims and Native Americans at one big happy table. In 1621, 53 Pilgrims and about 90 Wampanoag men feasted for three days. The word Thanksgiving came later.

The land was empty because plague had already killed up to nine in ten of the Massachusett. Tisquantum was kidnapped in 1614 and sold as a slave in Spain, and came home to a village with nobody left.

The Wampanoag fed the Pilgrims and kept the peace for decades. Then, in 1623, Myles Standish brought back a Native warrior's head, and it went on the fence at Plymouth's gate.

In 1637 English soldiers surrounded the Pequot village at Mystic, blocked both exits and set it on fire. Four hundred to seven hundred people died, women and children among them. Then the churches held a day of thanksgiving for the victory.

In 1676 Metacom, Massasoit's own son, was killed and his head stood on a pole in Plymouth for twenty years or more. His wife and son were sold into slavery. In 1970 Frank James was banned from giving his speech, so he gave it on Cole's Hill. It was the first National Day of Mourning.

One side got a feast. The other got buried. Which one were you taught?

Follow @UnbrokenLegacy.

The land was empty because plague had already killed up to nine in ten of the Massachusett. Tisquantum was kidnapped in 1614 and sold as a slave in Spain, and came home to a village with nobody left.

The Wampanoag fed the Pilgrims and kept the peace for decades. Then, in 1623, Myles Standish brought back a Native warrior's head, and it went on the fence at Plymouth's gate.

In 1637 English soldiers surrounded the Pequot village at Mystic, blocked both exits and set it on fire. Four hundred to seven hundred people died, women and children among them. Then the churches held a day of thanksgiving for the victory.

In 1676 Metacom, Massasoit's own son, was killed and his head stood on a pole in Plymouth for twenty years or more. His wife and son were sold into slavery. In 1970 Frank James was banned from giving his speech, so he gave it on Cole's Hill. It was the first National Day of Mourning.

One side got a feast. The other got buried. Which one were you taught?

snippet.title: How One Dive In Greece Started The World's Biggest Cleanup
snippet.description:
Halfway between Hawaii and California, giant ocean currents trap everything that floats. About 100,000 tonnes of plastic have gathered there, in a patch three times the size of France.

In 2011 a Dutch boy, Boyan Slat, went diving in Greece and saw more plastic bags than fish. He quit university, 38,000 people donated to his plan, and in 2018 his giant floating trap reached the patch. Then it broke. His next machines caught tonnes of plastic, but after years at sea that was still under one percent, and more kept coming. So he went to the source: just over 1,000 rivers carry 80 percent of the river plastic into the ocean. His first river fence in Guatemala was torn apart by a flash flood; the next barrier let the water flow under it and held. Today his team has pulled over 70 million kilos of trash out of rivers and the sea, a record 121 million dollar gift is paying for barriers in cities around the world, and the goal is 30 cities by 2030.

snippet.title: Here are the THREE SADDEST moments of the TRUMP family Thanksgiving
snippet.description:
📅 November 27, 2026

🦃🏰 The Trumps had Thanksgiving at Mar-a-Lago and it was, as usual, a disaster. Here are the three worst moments from their turkey day. 👇

1️⃣ DON JR.'S NOSE
Footage from the Mar-a-Lago dinner shows Donald Trump Jr. fiddling with his nose. 👃 Legally I have no opinion on this. Probably just an itch. 🤷

2️⃣ THE GILDED ENTRANCE
Trump entered the chandelier-lit Mar-a-Lago ballroom to applause from members of a club that costs $1 million to join and about $20,000 a year in dues. 💰 Gold-colored cutlery, towering candelabras, a pumpkin-covered archway. 🎃 Meanwhile, the cost of Thanksgiving dinner went up for regular American families. Let 'em eat cake! 🍰

3️⃣ THE TROOPS
On his Thanksgiving call with deployed service members, Trump told an Army air defense unit deployed across the Middle East since March: "You're going to continue that deployment, and we have victory at hand. It's going to be... whenever I want it to be, to be honest." 🪖 Imagine hearing that from your commander in chief on Thanksgiving. 😶

🥧 But when asked his favorite Thanksgiving dessert, he had an answer ready: pumpkin pie, with vanilla ice cream on top. He knew his favorite pie. He just didn't know when your kid's coming home.

🎖️ Thank you to every service member spending this holiday away from home. You deserve better than "whenever I want."

snippet.title: 🥃 How Glass Tumblers Are Made In A Factory
snippet.description:
Ever wondered how raw sand is transformed into the crystal-clear glass tumblers you use every day? Step inside a high-tech manufacturing facility to witness the incredible industrial process of molten glass production. From the initial melting of sand at extreme temperatures to the precision molding and flame-polishing stages, this video covers the entire journey of glass creation. 

You will see how automated mechanical shears cut glowing gobs of liquid glass, which are then expertly shaped by plungers and cooled to perfection. Watch as the tumblers travel along a conveyor belt, passing through intense flames to achieve their signature clarity and finish. The combination of intense heat, rhythmic mechanical movements, and cooling air streams creates a fascinating display of modern engineering and craftsmanship. This behind-the-scenes look offers a satisfying deep dive into the precision required to produce high-quality glassware at an industrial scale. Experience the transformation from incandescent liquid to a pristine, functional object ready for your home.
